source.title: Lisburn Standard, 11 October 1946, p. 2 ("Hillsborough Council: Mr. Joseph Orr, J.P., Re-elected Chairman"); Dromore Weekly Times and West Down Herald, 21 September 1946, p. 5; Belfast News-Letter, 4 October 1946, p. 3 ("County Down")
source.publisher: Lisburn Standard (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed: two nominations for Breda (Dromore Weekly Times, 21 September 1946, p. 5), but the only poll for the council was in Hillsborough division (Belfast News-Letter, 4 October 1946, p. 3); at the council's first meeting on Tuesday 8 October 1946 S. D. Stewart was among the members present and was welcomed with Fullerton (Blaris) and M'Gowan (Ballykeel) as 'the new members of the Council', while J. A. M'Kinstry was co-opted (Lisburn Standard, 11 October 1946, p. 2; read on the BNA page image)

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 3 October 1946. The only poll was in Hillsborough division (Belfast News-Letter, 4 October 1946, p. 3); Breda, where two were nominated, was therefore not polled and S. D. Stewart sat for it as a new member from the first meeting; thirteen other divisions were unopposed, and Ballymacbrennan and Carryduff had no nominations, so no member was elected for them (the council co-opted J. A. M'Kinstry, W. S. Patterson and G. C. Bell on 8 October 1946; co-options are not elections) (meetings pass, 7 Nov 2026). Division from the nominations: Stewart was one of the two Breda nominees and the only new member present who was not returned for another division; M'Kinstry, the other Breda nominee, was co-opted, which is not an election. The withdrawal itself is not printed. Returned unopposed.
